context.description: Build context directory, relative to the app root (the app path in the repository). Defaults to ".".

dockerfile.description: Path to a Dockerfile, relative to the app root. When set, the image is built from this Dockerfile instead of railpack auto-detection.

args.description: Build-time ARG values passed to the Dockerfile build (at most 32). Keys must be valid Dockerfile ARG names. Not available to the running app: use env for runtime variables.

build.description: How the container image is built from a Git repository. A canette.yaml committed to the repository wins field by field over the app's stored canette config. No effect for apps deployed from a container image.

port.description: Port the app listens on inside the container. canette also sets the PORT environment variable to this value. Overrides the port set in the UI.

command.description: Command that starts the app, as a list of arguments. Replaces the image's default entrypoint and command.

env.description: Plaintext environment variables, safe to commit. Merged on top of the env vars set in the canette UI (canette.yaml wins on conflicts). Use secrets in the UI for sensitive values. PORT is reserved: canette sets it from runtime.port.

cpu.description: CPU as a Kubernetes quantity, e.g. "100m" (0.1 core) or 1.

memory.description: Memory as a Kubernetes quantity, e.g. "128Mi" or "1Gi" (binary units), or a plain number of bytes. "MB"/"GB" are not valid: use "M"/"G" or "Mi"/"Gi".

requests.description: Resources reserved for the container; used by Kubernetes for scheduling.

cpu.description: CPU as a Kubernetes quantity, e.g. "100m" (0.1 core) or 1.

memory.description: Memory as a Kubernetes quantity, e.g. "128Mi" or "1Gi" (binary units), or a plain number of bytes. "MB"/"GB" are not valid: use "M"/"G" or "Mi"/"Gi".

limits.description: Maximum resources the container may use. Exceeding the memory limit restarts the container; CPU is throttled.

resources.description: CPU and memory requests and limits for the app's container, as Kubernetes quantities. Fields left out fall back to the platform defaults set by the canette admin (100m/128Mi requests and 500m/512Mi limits out of the box).

replicas.description: Number of pods to run, from 1 to 20 (higher values are capped at 20). Defaults to 1.

path.description: HTTP path that returns a 2xx or 3xx status when the app is healthy. Defaults to "/".

port.description: Port to probe. Defaults to the app's port.

initial_delay.description: Seconds to wait after the container starts before the first probe. Defaults to 5.

healthcheck.description: HTTP readiness probe for the app's container. While it fails, the pod gets no traffic, but it is never restarted. Without this block no probe is configured. An empty block (healthcheck: {}) enables the probe with the defaults below.

enabled.description: Whether the app gets a public URL. false keeps the app reachable inside the cluster through its Service but creates no HTTPRoute, the same as the "private" deployment type. Defaults to true for web apps.

ingress.description: Public HTTP routing for a web app.

hardened.description: Turns on hardened mode. The app container then runs as a non-root user (UID and GID 10001 unless user is set), with a read-only root filesystem (only writable_paths are writable) and all Linux capabilities dropped. Volumes are made writable for that user through the pod's fsGroup. Works for most app images, including railpack builds, whose files only need to be world-readable. Breaks images that need root at startup. Whether a port below 1024 (such as the default nginx image's port 80) works depends on the cluster's container runtime, so use a port of 1024 or higher, for example nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged on port 8080. Directories the app writes to must be listed in writable_paths or be a canette volume. Defaults to false.

writable_paths.description: Absolute directories that stay writable on top of the read-only root filesystem. Each one is an empty, pod-local directory (Kubernetes emptyDir) whose contents are lost when the pod restarts, and hides what the image has at that path. Defaults to ["/tmp"]; an empty list means no writable directories. A volume configured in canette on the same path takes precedence. Only used when hardened is true and read_only_root_filesystem is not false.

read_only_root_filesystem.description: Set to false to keep the root filesystem writable in hardened mode, for apps that write in many places. The other hardened settings still apply. Defaults to true. Only used when hardened is true.

user.description: UID and GID the container runs as in hardened mode, also used as the pod's fsGroup. Overrides the image's USER. Set it to the image's own non-root UID when the app's files are not readable by other users. Must not be 0 (root). Defaults to 10001. Only used when hardened is true.

security.description: Opt-in container hardening. Off unless security.hardened is true.

secrets.description: Names of the secrets the app expects, for documentation only. Secret values are never stored in canette.yaml: set them in the canette UI or API, where they are encrypted at rest and injected as environment variables at deploy time.

title: canette.yaml
description: Build and runtime configuration for a canette app, committed to the app's repository or set as the app's canette config. All fields are optional: absence means "use platform defaults". Unknown fields are ignored.
